items.s: First journey · leg 1 of 15 · by land
tx: Antioch down the Orontes to Seleucia. From the Acts 13-14 map: the valley of the Orontes.
items.note: They go down to Antioch's port.

items.s: First journey · leg 2 of 15 · by sea
items.note: They sail to Cyprus and preach in the synagogues.

items.s: First journey · leg 3 of 15 · by land
tx: Across Cyprus, Salamis to Paphos. From the Acts 13-14 map: the coast road by Kition and Kourion.
items.note: Gone through the island: Bar Jesus, and the proconsul Sergius Paulus.

items.s: First journey · leg 4 of 15 · by sea
tx: Ours: it keeps to the sea, past the capes and islands on the way.
items.note: They sail to Perga in Pamphylia; John leaves them for Jerusalem. Perga stands inland, and where they landed isn't said.

items.s: First journey · leg 5 of 15 · by land
tx: The Via Sebaste, Perga to Antioch of Pisidia. From the Acts 13-14 map: Augustus's road, by French's survey.
items.note: The sermon in the synagogue, and two Sabbaths.

items.s: First journey · leg 6 of 15 · by land
tx: Antioch of Pisidia to Iconium. From the Acts 13-14 map.
items.note: A long stay, until a move to stone them.

items.s: First journey · leg 7 of 15 · by land
tx: Iconium to Lystra. From the Acts 13-14 map.
items.note: The lame man healed; Paul stoned (14:19).

items.s: First journey · leg 8 of 15 · by land
tx: Lystra to Derbe. From the Acts 13-14 map.
items.note: He goes out with Barnabas the next day.

items.s: First journey · leg 9 of 15 · by land
tx: Lystra to Derbe. From the Acts 13-14 map.
items.note: They go back.

items.s: First journey · leg 10 of 15 · by land
tx: Iconium to Lystra. From the Acts 13-14 map.
items.note: They go back.

items.s: First journey · leg 11 of 15 · by land
tx: Antioch of Pisidia to Iconium. From the Acts 13-14 map.
items.note: Elders appointed in every assembly.

items.s: First journey · leg 12 of 15 · by land
tx: The Via Sebaste, Perga to Antioch of Pisidia. From the Acts 13-14 map: Augustus's road, by French's survey.
items.note: Through Pisidia to Pamphylia; they speak the word in Perga.

items.s: First journey · leg 13 of 15 · by land
tx: Perga to Attalia. From the Acts 13-14 map.
items.note: They go down to the port.

items.s: First journey · leg 14 of 15 · by sea · not all stated
tx: Ours: it keeps to the sea, past the capes and islands on the way.
items.note: They sail to Antioch: the port, Seleucia, isn't named this time.

items.s: First journey · leg 15 of 15 · by land
tx: Antioch down the Orontes to Seleucia. From the Acts 13-14 map: the valley of the Orontes.
items.note: They gather the assembly and tell what God had done.

items.s: Second journey · leg 1 of 21 · by land · not all stated
tx: Antioch through the Syrian and Cilician Gates to Derbe. Sure as far as Podandus, below the Cilician Gates. Beyond, the road to Derbe is not attested: Ulukisla only marks the way.
items.note: He goes through Syria and Cilicia. Tarsus isn't named; the road to Derbe ran by it and through the Cilician Gates.

items.s: Second journey · leg 2 of 21 · by land
tx: Antioch through the Syrian and Cilician Gates to Derbe. Sure as far as Podandus, below the Cilician Gates. Beyond, the road to Derbe is not attested: Ulukisla only marks the way.

items.s: Second journey · leg 3 of 21 · by land
tx: Lystra to Derbe. From the Acts 13-14 map.
items.note: Timothy joins them.

items.s: Second journey · leg 4 of 21 · by land · not all stated
tx: Iconium to Lystra. From the Acts 13-14 map.
items.note: Named only as where Timothy was known; going through the cities implies they came.

items.s: Second journey · leg 5 of 21 · by land · not all stated
tx: Antioch of Pisidia to Iconium. From the Acts 13-14 map.
items.note: Not named: they went through the cities, and the region of Phrygia and Galatia.

items.s: Second journey · leg 6 of 21 · by land · not all stated
items.note: Forbidden to speak in Asia, they come opposite Mysia and try for Bithynia. No town is named, and the way isn't known.

items.s: Second journey · leg 7 of 21 · by land · not all stated
items.note: Passing by Mysia, they come down to Troas: the vision of the man of Macedonia, and 'we' begins.

items.s: Second journey · leg 8 of 21 · by sea
tx: Ours: it keeps to the sea, past the capes and islands on the way.
items.note: A straight course.

items.s: Second journey · leg 9 of 21 · by sea
items.note: The next day.

items.s: Second journey · leg 10 of 21 · by land
tx: The Via Egnatia, Neapolis to Thessalonica. Sure in outline: Strabo, milestones, and the itineraries' stations, with Acts 17:1's own Philippi, Amphipolis and Apollonia.
items.note: A Roman colony: Lydia, the slave girl, the prison and the earthquake (16:13-40).

items.s: Second journey · leg 11 of 21 · by land
tx: The Via Egnatia, Neapolis to Thessalonica. Sure in outline: Strabo, milestones, and the itineraries' stations, with Acts 17:1's own Philippi, Amphipolis and Apollonia.
items.note: Passed through, on the Via Egnatia.

items.s: Second journey · leg 12 of 21 · by land
tx: The Via Egnatia, Neapolis to Thessalonica. Sure in outline: Strabo, milestones, and the itineraries' stations, with Acts 17:1's own Philippi, Amphipolis and Apollonia.
items.note: Passed through.

items.s: Second journey · leg 13 of 21 · by land
tx: The Via Egnatia, Neapolis to Thessalonica. Sure in outline: Strabo, milestones, and the itineraries' stations, with Acts 17:1's own Philippi, Amphipolis and Apollonia.
items.note: Three Sabbaths in the synagogue; Jason's house.

items.s: Second journey · leg 14 of 21 · by land
tx: Thessalonica to Beroea. Not attested by any itinerary: across the Macedonian plain by the Roman bridge at Kleidi.
items.note: Sent away by night.

items.s: Second journey · leg 15 of 21 · by sea · not all stated
tx: Ours: it keeps to the sea, past the capes and islands on the way.
items.note: Sent 'as far as to the sea', then brought to Athens: by sea is the usual reading, but neither the port nor the way is said.

items.s: Second journey · leg 16 of 21 · by land · not all stated
tx: Ours: the text doesn't give the way, and the line only keeps to the land.
items.note: He leaves Athens for Corinth, by land or sea it doesn't say. He stays a year and six months (18:11).

items.s: Second journey · leg 17 of 21 · by land
items.note: Corinth's eastern port: he shaves his head for a vow.

items.s: Second journey · leg 18 of 21 · by sea
tx: Ours: it keeps to the sea, past the capes and islands on the way.
items.note: He sails for Syria with Priscilla and Aquila, and leaves them at Ephesus.

items.s: Second journey · leg 19 of 21 · by sea · not all stated
tx: Ours: it keeps to the sea, past the capes and islands on the way.
items.note: He lands at Caesarea. The course isn't given.

items.s: Second journey · leg 20 of 21 · by land · not all stated
tx: Caesarea to Jerusalem. By Antipatris (23:31) and Beth Horon, the soldiers' road.
items.note: He goes up and greets the assembly: Jerusalem isn't named, but in 18:21 he says he must keep the coming feast there.

items.s: Second journey · leg 21 of 21 · by land · not all stated
tx: Ours: the text doesn't give the way, and the line only keeps to the land.
items.note: He goes down to Antioch. The way isn't said.

items.s: Third journey · leg 1 of 25 · by land · not all stated
tx: Antioch through the Syrian and Cilician Gates to Derbe. Sure as far as Podandus, below the Cilician Gates. Beyond, the road to Derbe is not attested: Ulukisla only marks the way.
items.note: Not named: the road to Galatia ran through Cilicia, as in 15:41.

items.s: Third journey · leg 2 of 25 · by land · not all stated
tx: Antioch through the Syrian and Cilician Gates to Derbe. Sure as far as Podandus, below the Cilician Gates. Beyond, the road to Derbe is not attested: Ulukisla only marks the way.
items.note: He goes through the region of Galatia and Phrygia in order. No town is named.

items.s: Third journey · leg 3 of 25 · by land · not all stated
tx: Lystra to Derbe. From the Acts 13-14 map.
items.note: Not named.

items.s: Third journey · leg 4 of 25 · by land · not all stated
tx: Iconium to Lystra. From the Acts 13-14 map.
items.note: Not named.

items.s: Third journey · leg 5 of 25 · by land · not all stated
tx: Antioch of Pisidia to Iconium. From the Acts 13-14 map.
items.note: Not named.

items.s: Third journey · leg 6 of 25 · by land · not all stated
items.note: Having passed through the upper country, which way isn't said. About three years here (19:8-10; 20:31). The common road ran by Colossae and Laodicea, but Colossians 2:1 suggests he never saw them.

items.s: Third journey · leg 7 of 25 · by land · not all stated
tx: Ours: the text doesn't give the way, and the line only keeps to the land.
items.note: Acts says only that he left for Macedonia; 2 Corinthians 2:12 puts him at Troas on the way. By land or sea isn't said.

items.s: Third journey · leg 8 of 25 · by sea · not all stated
tx: Ours: it keeps to the sea, past the capes and islands on the way.
items.note: He goes through those parts. No town is named.

items.s: Third journey · leg 9 of 25 · by land · not all stated
tx: Ours: the text doesn't give the way, and the line only keeps to the land.
items.note: He comes into Greece and spends three months there: Corinth is inferred (1 Cor 16:5-6; Rom 16:1, 23). A plot, as he is about to sail for Syria.

items.s: Third journey · leg 10 of 25 · by land · not all stated
tx: Ours: the text doesn't give the way, and the line only keeps to the land.
items.note: He returns through Macedonia; his companions are listed in 20:4. After the days of Unleavened Bread.

items.s: Third journey · leg 11 of 25 · by land · not all stated
tx: The Via Egnatia, Neapolis to Thessalonica. Sure in outline: Strabo, milestones, and the itineraries' stations, with Acts 17:1's own Philippi, Amphipolis and Apollonia.
items.note: 'We sailed away from Philippi': its port was Neapolis (16:11).

items.s: Third journey · leg 12 of 25 · by sea
tx: Ours: it keeps to the sea, past the capes and islands on the way.
items.note: Five days at sea, seven days at Troas: Eutychus.

items.s: Third journey · leg 13 of 25 · by land
tx: Troas to Assos. No Roman road is attested; the line keeps inland by the villages and the bridge below Assos.
items.note: Paul goes on foot while the others sail round; they take him aboard at Assos.

items.s: Third journey · leg 14 of 25 · by sea
Third journey · leg 15 of 25 · by sea
tx: Ours: it keeps to the sea, past the capes and islands on the way.
items.note: The next day they come opposite Chios: passed, not landed.

items.s: Third journey · leg 16 of 25 · by sea
tx: Ours: it keeps to the sea, past the capes and islands on the way.
items.note: They touch at Samos.

items.s: Third journey · leg 17 of 25 · by sea
items.note: 'And stayed at Trogyllium': in the WEB, though not in the oldest manuscripts.

items.s: Third journey · leg 18 of 25 · by sea
tx: Ours: it keeps to the sea, past the capes and islands on the way.
items.note: He sails past Ephesus (20:16) and calls its elders to Miletus.

items.s: Third journey · leg 19 of 25 · by sea
tx: Ours: it keeps to the sea, past the capes and islands on the way.
items.note: A straight course.

items.s: Third journey · leg 20 of 25 · by sea
tx: Ours: it keeps to the sea, past the capes and islands on the way.
items.note: The next day.

items.s: Third journey · leg 21 of 25 · by sea
items.note: They find a ship crossing over to Phoenicia.

items.s: Third journey · leg 22 of 25 · by sea
tx: Ours: it keeps to the sea, past the capes and islands on the way.
items.note: In sight of Cyprus, they leave it on the left hand, and land at Tyre: seven days there.

items.s: Third journey · leg 23 of 25 · by sea
tx: Ours: it keeps to the sea, past the capes and islands on the way.
items.note: They finish the voyage from Tyre, and stay one day.

items.s: Third journey · leg 24 of 25 · by land · not all stated
tx: Ptolemais to Caesarea. Along the coast, under Mount Carmel.
items.note: The way isn't said; by the coast road, most likely. Philip's house, and Agabus.

items.s: Third journey · leg 25 of 25 · by land
tx: Caesarea to Jerusalem. By Antipatris (23:31) and Beth Horon, the soldiers' road.
items.note: They go up to Jerusalem, to lodge with Mnason of Cyprus.

items.s: Voyage to Rome · leg 1 of 13 · by sea
tx: Ours: it keeps to the sea, past the capes and islands on the way.
items.note: The next day; Julius lets Paul go to his friends.

items.s: Voyage to Rome · leg 2 of 13 · by sea
tx: Ours: it keeps to the sea, past the capes and islands on the way.
items.note: Under the lee of Cyprus, as the winds were against them, then across the sea off Cilicia and Pamphylia to Myra: a ship of Alexandria, sailing for Italy. Which side of Cyprus is inferred.

items.s: Voyage to Rome · leg 3 of 13 · by sea
tx: Ours: it keeps to the sea, past the capes and islands on the way.
items.note: Slowly, many days, and with difficulty opposite Cnidus: passed, not landed.

items.s: Voyage to Rome · leg 4 of 13 · by sea
items.note: The wind not allowing them further, they sail under the lee of Crete, opposite Salmone.

items.s: Voyage to Rome · leg 5 of 13 · by sea
tx: Ours: it keeps to the sea, past the capes and islands on the way.
items.note: Near the city of Lasea. Most advise going on to winter at Phoenix, a port of Crete; they never reach it.

items.s: Voyage to Rome · leg 6 of 13 · by sea
items.note: Along Crete, close in, until the Euroclydon drives them; under the lee of Clauda they secure the boat and fear the Syrtis.

items.s: Voyage to Rome · leg 7 of 13 · by sea · not all stated
items.note: Fourteen nights driven back and forth in the Adriatic Sea: the course isn't given. The bay where two seas met (27:41) is, by tradition, St Paul's Bay. Three months on the island.

items.s: Voyage to Rome · leg 8 of 13 · by sea
tx: Ours: it keeps to the sea, past the capes and islands on the way.
items.note: In a ship of Alexandria, the Twin Brothers: three days.

items.s: Voyage to Rome · leg 9 of 13 · by sea
items.note: They circle round to Rhegium.

items.s: Voyage to Rome · leg 10 of 13 · by sea
tx: Ours: it keeps to the sea, past the capes and islands on the way.
items.note: A south wind; the second day. Brothers, and seven days.

items.n: Puteoli to The Market of Appius
items.s: Voyage to Rome · leg 11 of 13 · by land
tx: The Via Campana and the Via Appia, Puteoli to Rome. Sure: the Via Appia's stations, among them the Market of Appius and the Three Taverns (28:15).
items.note: Brothers from Rome come out to meet them.

items.n: The Market of Appius to The Three Taverns
items.s: Voyage to Rome · leg 12 of 13 · by land
tx: The Via Campana and the Via Appia, Puteoli to Rome. Sure: the Via Appia's stations, among them the Market of Appius and the Three Taverns (28:15).
items.note: The brothers from Rome come out as far as here, too, to meet them: the verse names both places.

items.s: Voyage to Rome · leg 13 of 13 · by land
tx: The Via Campana and the Via Appia, Puteoli to Rome. Sure: the Via Appia's stations, among them the Market of Appius and the Three Taverns (28:15).
items.note: Paul is allowed to stay by himself, with the soldier who guards him.

dims: Old walled city of Damascus, Syria
tx: The name and occupation are continuous, and the Roman grid (the street called Straight, Acts 9:11) survives in the old city.
Syria; held by King Aretas's governor (2 Cor 11:32)
items.note: Conversion on the road (9:3); let down the wall in a basket (9:25; 2 Cor 11:32-33); returned there from Arabia (Gal 1:17).

First visit 9:26-29; famine visit 12:25; council 15:2-4. The end of journey 2 is only implied (18:22 says he went up and greeted the assembly). Journey 3 ends here (21:15-17) with the arrest (21:31-33) that leads to Rome.

tx: The name never changed; Herod's harbour city is excavated (Pilate inscription).
items.note: Sent off from here to Tarsus (9:30); landed here at the end of journey 2 (18:22); stayed with Philip on journey 3 (21:8); held two years (24:27). The voyage to Italy starts from here, implied in 27:1-2.

dims: Tel Afek at the Yarkon springs, Rosh HaAyin, Israel
tx: Herod's city at the Yarkon springs is certain (Josephus; excavations).
items.note: Night stage of the escort from Jerusalem to Caesarea (23:31-33).

tx: Continuous name and city; the Roman city (paved street, Gozlukule mound) lies under the modern town.
items.note: Paul's home city. The coordinate is the town item's and is precise only to the minute. Journey 2 crosses Cilicia (15:41) without naming the city.

tx: Continuous city (Antakya) on the Orontes; Seleucid and Roman capital of Syria.
Antioch of Syria, Antioch on the Orontes, Antakya
items.note: Barnabas brings Saul here (11:25-26). It is the home base where journeys 1 and 2 start and end and journey 3 starts (13:1-3; 14:26; 15:35-40; 18:22-23). Antioch in Acts 13:14, 14:19, 14:21 and 2 Tim 3:11 is Pisidian Antioch.

tx: Antioch's harbour; ruins and the Titus tunnel at Cevlik.
items.note: Port of embarkation for Cyprus.
Landing on Cyprus; preaching in the synagogues.

dims: Paphos Archaeological Park, Kato Paphos, Cyprus
tx: New Paphos was the Roman capital of Cyprus and seat of the proconsul (Sergius Paulus, 13:7); excavated.
Nea Paphos, New Paphos, Kato Paphos

dims: Perge ruins at Aksu, near Antalya, Turkey
items.note: John Mark leaves the party here (13:13); on the way back they preach here (14:25).
They sail from here back to Antioch (14:26).

tx: Roman colony identified by inscriptions; excavated.
Pisidia (Acts 13:14; 14:24); in the province of Galatia
items.note: Synagogue sermon (13:16-41). The WEB calls it simply Antioch in 14:19, 14:21 and 2 Tim 3:11. Journey 2 probably passes nearby (16:6) but doesn't name it.

tx: Continuous name (Konya); the ancient mound is Alaeddin hill.
Province of Galatia; Acts 14:6 treats it as outside Lycaonia

dims: Zoldera mound near Hatunsaray, Konya, Turkey
tx: In 1885 Sterrett found the colony's Latin dedication naming Lystra on the site.
The Zoldera mound, by Wikipedia's coordinate
items.note: Paul is hailed as Mercury and then stoned here (14:12, 19). Timothy's home (16:1).

dims: Kerti Hoyuk, north-east of Karaman, Turkey
tx: A dedication naming Derbe, found in 1956, points to Kerti Hoyuk. The rival is Devri Sehri, a few km to the south-east, backed by a later inscription. Ramsay's older choice, Gudelisin, is abandoned.
items.note: Gaius of Derbe: 20:4.

tx: Roman colony Alexandria Troas; ruins on the coast. It is not Troy.
items.note: Here Paul has the vision of the man of Macedonia (16:9), Eutychus falls (20:9-12), and the cloak is left with Carpus (2 Tim 4:13).

tx: The island is certain; the point is the ancient city and harbour on its north coast, the natural overnight anchorage.
North Aegean (Thrace); not named in the WEB
Port of Philippi on the Via Egnatia; continuous town (Kavala).
items.note: The return sailing in Acts 20:6 (from Philippi) used this port too, but the verse doesn't name it.

tx: Philippians addressed to the saints at Philippi (Phil 1:1)
items.note: Lydia and the jailer (16:14-34). Philippians is written in bonds (Phil 1:7, 13) but doesn't name the city it was written from.

tx: Excavated city on the Strymon; name preserved.
items.note: Passed through on the Via Egnatia.

dims: Near Nea Apollonia, south of Lake Volvi, Greece
tx: The Via Egnatia station south of Lake Bolbe is fixed by the itineraries, but the town is unexcavated and the exact spot is uncertain.
Continuous city; the point is its Roman forum.
1 and 2 Thessalonians addressed to the assembly of the Thessalonians (1 Thess 1:1; 2 Thess 1:1)
items.note: Aristarchus of Thessalonica sails with Paul (27:2).
The WEB spells it Beroea, not Berea. Sopater of Beroea: 20:4.

tx: Continuous city; the point is the agora, where Paul reasoned daily (17:17), below the Areopagus (17:19, 22).
items.note: In 1 Thess 3:1 Paul recalls being left behind at Athens alone.

tx: Excavated Roman colony beneath Acrocorinth (Gallio inscription at Delphi dates the stay).

1 and 2 Corinthians addressed to the assembly of God at Corinth (1 Cor 1:2; 2 Cor 1:1). Romans is usually placed here (Phoebe of Cenchreae, Rom 16:1; Erastus the city treasurer, Rom 16:23, with 2 Tim 4:20), but the letter does not name the city.
items.note: Paul stays 18 months (18:11). The three months in Greece on journey 3 (20:2-3) are generally Corinth, but the WEB says only Greece.

tx: Corinth's Saronic Gulf harbour; excavated harbour works at Kechries.
Romans commends Phoebe of the assembly at Cenchreae (Rom 16:1)
items.note: Paul shaves his head here for a vow (18:18).

tx: Excavated city; the theatre of Acts 19:29 stands.

1 Corinthians written from Ephesus (1 Cor 16:8; cf. 16:19). Ephesians addressed to the saints at Ephesus (Eph 1:1). 1 Timothy addressed to Timothy, left at Ephesus (1 Tim 1:3). The first of the seven letters (Rev 2:1).
items.note: Brief stop on journey 2 (18:19-21); two to three years on journey 3 (19:10; 20:31); sailed past (20:16), elders called to Miletus (20:17). The words at Ephesus in Eph 1:1 are missing from some early manuscripts; the WEB has them.

tx: Excavated city with its harbour below; name preserved.
items.note: Paul walks from Troas and boards the ship here.

tx: Continuous city, chief town of Lesbos.
Asia (island of Lesbos, not named in the WEB)
items.note: The WEB spells it Mitylene.

tx: The island is certain; the ship only came opposite it (20:15), presumably through the strait on its east side.
items.note: Passed by, not landed.

tx: The ancient city and harbour of Samos, at Pythagoreio.
items.note: Touched at, not stayed.

dims: Tip of the Dilek (Mycale) peninsula, Aydin, Turkey, facing Samos
tx: Strabo's Trogilium is the Mycale promontory across the strait from Samos, but the exact anchorage is unknown.
Cape Mycale, the tip of the promontory
items.note: The WEB names it: 'and stayed at Trogyllium'. The clause is missing from the oldest manuscripts but present in the Majority Text that the WEB follows.

dims: Ruins at Balat, Didim, Aydin, Turkey
tx: Excavated city; its theatre and harbours are now silted inland.
items.note: Farewell to the Ephesian elders (20:17-38); Trophimus left sick here (2 Tim 4:20).

tx: The ancient city of Kos, under and beside the modern town.
The ancient city at the island's north tip, under the modern town.

dims: Patara ruins near Gelemis, Antalya, Turkey
tx: Excavated Lycian harbour city; name preserved.
items.note: They change here to a ship bound for Phoenicia (21:2).
Seven days with the disciples; prayer on the beach (21:4-5). Acts 12:20 names Tyre in a story without Paul.

tx: Continuous name (Akko); renamed Ptolemais under the Ptolemies.

items.note: Julius lets Paul visit friends here. Acts 12:20 names Sidon in a story without Paul.

tx: Excavated Lycian city (rock tombs, theatre); its harbour was Andriake, about 5 km away.
items.note: They change here to the Alexandrian grain ship (27:6).

dims: Knidos ruins at Tekir, tip of the Datca peninsula, Turkey
tx: The Hellenistic and Roman city with its two harbours at Tekir. An earlier city may have stood at Burgaz near Datca, but by Paul's day Cnidus was at Tekir.
Asia (Caria; not named in the WEB)
items.note: Came with difficulty opposite it; the wind kept them from going further, and they did not land.

dims: Cape Sideros, north-east tip of Crete, Greece
tx: The ancient Samonion/Salmonion promontory is usually Cape Sidero; a minority prefer a cape a little further south on Crete's east coast.
items.note: The ship passes opposite it into the lee of Crete.

dims: Kaloi Limenes, south coast of Heraklion, Crete
tx: The name survives as Kaloi Limenes, a bay on Crete's south coast just east of Cape Lithino.
items.note: Paul warns against sailing on from here (27:9-10). Acts 27:12 calls it the haven. The item is the modern village and port.

dims: Ruins east of Kaloi Limenes, Crete
tx: Ruins about 2 km east of Kaloi Limenes have been taken as Lasea since the 19th century. Manuscripts spell the name variously (Lasaea, Alassa, Thalassa).
items.note: Named only as the city near Fair Havens.

dims: Loutro / Phoinikas, near Chora Sfakion, Crete
tx: The ancient Phoenix lies on the Mouros headland at Loutro. Scholars dispute whether the harbour is Loutro bay or Phineka bay on the west side of the headland, since the WEB says it looks northeast and southeast.
items.note: Their goal, never reached: the Euroclydon drove them off (27:14-15).

dims: Gavdos island, south of Crete, Greece
tx: Name continuity (Kaudos, Gavdos), and its position in the storm's track fits.
items.note: Under its lee they secure the boat and undergird the ship. The WEB spells it Clauda; many manuscripts have Cauda.

dims: Malta (traditional landing at St Paul's Bay)
tx: The traditional identification is Malta, with the wreck at St Paul's Bay or St Paul's Islands.
Not named; the ship is driven across the Adriatic Sea (27:27), which in antiquity meant the open central Mediterranean
items.note: The WEB has Malta, not Melita. Three months here, and Publius (28:7-11).
Three days.

tx: Continuous city on the Strait of Messina.
items.note: They wait a day here for a south wind.

dims: Pozzuoli (Rione Terra), Bay of Naples, Italy
tx: Continuous town. Rione Terra is the acropolis of the Roman colony, above the harbour where the grain ships docked.
items.note: Seven days with the brothers (28:14, which continues the sentence without repeating the name).

tx: The Via Appia station at the 43rd mile, fixed by the itineraries and milestones; remains at Borgo Faiti.
Forum Appii, Appii Forum, Borgo Faiti
items.note: The brothers from Rome come out this far to meet Paul.

tx: A Via Appia station about the 33rd mile, near Cisterna; the itineraries fix it roughly, but the exact remains are uncertain.
items.note: Acts 28:15 has the brothers from Rome come out as far as the Market of Appius and the Three Taverns to meet Paul.

tx: Continuous city; the city item's point sits by the Forum.

Romans addressed to all in Rome (Rom 1:7, 15). 2 Timothy places Paul there in chains (2 Tim 1:16-17) but does not say it was written there. Philippians mentions Caesar's household (Phil 4:22), and Acts 28:30 has the two years in a rented house; both point to Rome without naming it.

dims: Ancient site at Oren, near Burhaniye, Balikesir, Turkey (modern Edremit lies inland)
tx: The Roman harbour town is placed on the coast at Oren (Karatas), and the name moved to inland Edremit.
Asia (Acts 27:2, places on the coast of Asia)
items.note: Named only as the home port of the first ship on the Rome voyage. Paul did not go there, so do not draw it as a stop.

tx: Continuous city; the Roman agora is excavated.
Revelation's letter to the assembly in Smyrna (Rev 2:8-11)
Excavated city (UNESCO); name preserved in Bergama.
Revelation's letter to the assembly in Pergamum (Rev 2:12-17)
items.note: The WEB spells it Pergamum.

tx: Inscriptions naming Thyatira found at Akhisar; the ruins lie in the town centre.
Revelation's letter to the assembly in Thyatira (Rev 2:18-29)
items.note: Lydia, the seller of purple at Philippi, came from Thyatira (Acts 16:14).

tx: Excavated Lydian capital; name preserved in Sart.
Revelation's letter to the assembly in Sardis (Rev 3:1-6)
The ancient city lies under Alasehir (Byzantine basilica piers survive).
Revelation's letter to the assembly in Philadelphia (Rev 3:7-13)
items.note: The coordinate is precise only to the minute (the same as the Alasehir town item).

dims: Ruins near Goncali / Eskihisar, Denizli, Turkey
tx: Excavated city on the Lycus; identification secure.
Revelation's letter to the assembly in Laodicea (Rev 3:14-22). Colossians is to be read in the assembly of the Laodiceans, and they are to read the letter from Laodicea (Col 4:16).

dims: Unexcavated mound north of Honaz, Denizli, Turkey
tx: The hoyuk on the Lycus near Honaz, identified from coins and inscriptions; not yet excavated.

Colossians addressed to the saints at Colossae (Col 1:2). Philemon is usually placed here: Onesimus is one of you (Col 4:9), and Archippus appears in Col 4:17 and Phlm 2. Philemon itself names no city.
Excavated city above the Pamukkale travertines (UNESCO).
items.note: Named only in Col 4:13 (Epaphras's zeal for it); none of the roles fits.

tx: Revelation, with its seven letters, written on Patmos (Rev 1:9-11)
items.note: John was on the isle when told to write and send to the seven assemblies (1:11).

dims: Ruins north of Preveza, Epirus, Greece
tx: Augustus's Actian Nicopolis in Epirus is the usual choice, as the leading city on the west coast for a winter stay. The rivals are Nicopolis on the Nestus in Thrace and a Nicopolis in Cilicia.
items.note: Paul plans to winter there and asks Titus to come, so the letter was not written there (the later subscription saying it was is not in the WEB). None of the roles fits.
Acts 20:2 calls it Greece.
The Roman province, on the Aegean shore of Asia Minor.
The Roman province reached south to Antioch of Pisidia, Iconium, Lystra and Derbe.
Romans 15:19's far point of Paul's preaching.

items.n: The sea off Cilicia and Pamphylia

items.note: In Paul's day the name reached south over the open sea between Crete, Sicily and Greece.
The shoals off Libya that the sailors feared (27:17).
Usually placed at Corinth, from Phoebe of Cenchreae (16:1) and Erastus (16:23), but the letter doesn't name the city.
Written from Macedonia, by 2 Corinthians 7:5 and 9:2, no town named.
'At Ephesus' is missing from some early manuscripts; the WEB has it.
To be read at Laodicea too (4:16).
To Timothy, whom Paul left at Ephesus.
To Titus, whom Paul left in Crete.

items.s: a letter to the seven assemblies
tx: Ephesus, Smyrna, Pergamum, Thyatira, Sardis, Philadelphia, Laodicea
